clinician.trajectory_summary: A 66-year-old woman with no prior medical history sustained blunt abdominal trauma from a motor vehicle collision and presented to the hospital in shock (systolic blood pressure 70 mmHg) with upper abdominal pain, tenderness, and peripheral cold sensations. Initial FAST examination was negative and plain radiographs of chest and pelvis were normal. Contrast-enhanced CT imaging revealed rib fractures, liver and splenic injuries, and critically, right gastric artery involvement with intra-abdominal hemorrhage and extravascular contrast leakage during the equilibrium phase. The patient was transferred to a tertiary center for definitive management. Angiography was performed and demonstrated irregularities in the diameter of the right gastric artery with structural damage (though active bleeding was not visualized on the angiogram itself). Coil embolization of the right gastric artery was performed to prevent rebleeding and pseudoaneurysm formation. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT on day 2 post-injury confirmed resolution of extravascular contrast leakage, absence of pseudoaneurysms, and reduction in hematoma volume. The patient recovered well and subsequently resumed daily activities without sequelae.
